## Overview

This unversioned [[adyen]] website-guide snapshot introduces 3D Secure 2 for merchant online-payment integrations and routes readers among native and redirect implementations, Sessions and Advanced server-side flows, authentication-flow explanations, and additional 3DS routes. It is the high-level source for [[adyen-3d-secure]], not version-qualified implementation evidence for the separately retained native SDKs.

## Key takeaways

- Adyen describes 3D Secure 2 as an extra verification layer for card-not-present transactions and recommends it for strong-customer-authentication regulations and liability-shift rules. The recommendation is not proof that a particular transaction complies, authenticates successfully, or receives liability shift.
- The guide presents **Native** authentication within a merchant website or mobile app and **Redirect** authentication on the issuer's site. It warns that redirect can reduce conversion because of technical errors or shopper abandonment.
- The documented routing depends on the merchant's server-side payments flow: Sessions has built-in 3D Secure 2 support without additional configuration, while Advanced routes readers by platform and Drop-in, Components, or API-only integration type. Native integrations using Checkout API v46 or earlier are sent to a separate earlier-version guide.
- A qualifying native 3D Secure transaction can be frictionless or require an issuer challenge. The page also links authorization-only, data-only, and standalone-authentication variants; its data-only description is limited to Visa and Mastercard.

> [!warning] Evidence boundary
> This collected page is high-level integration guidance. It does not establish current merchant, card, issuer, region, or account eligibility; prove production configuration, authentication, authorization, capture, settlement, or liability shift; or define the versioned native SDK runtime. Use [[adyen-3ds2-ios-sdk]] and [[adyen-3ds2-android-sdk]] only for their separately retained package-qualified native implementation evidence.

quotes.text: 3D Secure 2 is an authentication protocol that provides an additional layer of verification for card-not-present (CNP) transactions. We recommend that you use it to comply with regulations that require strong customer authentication for online payments such as [PSD2 SCA](/online-payments/psd2-sca-compliance-and-implementation-guide) in the [European Economic Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Economic_Area) and the Payment Services Regulations 2017 in the UK, and to use [liability shift rules](/online-payments/3d-secure-for-regulation-compliance#3dsecurechargebackliabilityshiftrules).

We support two 3D Secure 2 authentication implementations:

* **Native**: The card issuer performs the authentication within your website or mobile app using passive, biometric, and two-factor authentication approaches. For more information about the shopper experience, refer to [3D Secure 2 authentication flows](#authentication-flows).

* **Redirect**: Shoppers are redirected to the card issuer's site to provide additional authentication data, for example a password or an SMS verification code. The redirection might lead to lower conversion rates due to technical errors during the redirection, or shoppers dropping out of the authentication process.

* [**Sessions flow** ](/online-payments/build-your-integration#sessions-flow-a-single-api-request): You do not need additional configuration to support 3D Secure 2. The [Sessions flow integration](/online-payments/build-your-integration/sessions-flow) has built-in support for 3D Secure 2.
* [**Advanced flow** ](/online-payments/build-your-integration#advanced-flow-three-api-requests): Use the following guides to integrate with 3D Secure 2, selecting the platform (Web, iOS, or Android) and integration type (Drop-in or Components) that corresponds to your online payments integration. For an API-only integration, use the following guides to integrate with our pre-built 3D Secure 2 Component or Action Component.

When you have implemented native 3D Secure, a transaction that qualifies for 3D Secure 2 can go through either a [frictionless flow](#frictionless-flow) or a [challenge flow](#challenge-flow), depending on the issuer's requirements.
[Submit a 3D Secure 2 request without requesting for an authentication. Only available for Visa and Mastercard.](/online-payments/3d-secure/data-only)

## Adyen 3D Secure

Adyen's merchant-facing online-payments guide describes 3D Secure 2 as an additional verification layer for card-not-present transactions. It recommends 3DS2 in connection with strong-customer-authentication regulations and liability-shift rules, but the guide does not prove compliance, successful authentication, payment authorization, or liability shift for a particular transaction. [[source-adyen-docs-online-payments-3d-secure]]

## Merchant integration routes

The guide presents two implementation shapes: **Native**, where the issuer performs authentication within the merchant website or mobile app, and **Redirect**, where the shopper moves to the issuer's site. Adyen warns that redirect can lower conversion because of technical errors or shopper abandonment.

Server-side routing is separate from that shopper-facing distinction. Sessions has built-in 3D Secure 2 support without additional configuration. Advanced integrations are routed by Web, iOS, or Android and by Drop-in, Components, or API-only integration type. Native integrations using Checkout API v46 or earlier are routed to a separate earlier-version guide.

For a qualifying native transaction, issuer requirements determine whether the flow is frictionless or presents a challenge. The page also navigates to authorization-only, data-only, and standalone-authentication variants; the data-only description is limited to Visa and Mastercard.

## SDK evidence boundary

This concept covers the high-level merchant website guide across web and mobile integration choices. It does not replace [[adyen-3ds2-ios-sdk]] or [[adyen-3ds2-android-sdk]], which retain package-qualified native transaction, challenge, lifecycle, security, privacy, and UI evidence. Do not attribute those SDK-specific behaviors or versions to the unversioned website guide, and do not use SDK availability as proof of merchant enablement or payment outcome.
